# Incident Report — NetSupport RAT Infection (2024-11-26)

## 1. Infected/Victim Host

| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** | Source of all malicious traffic below |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.11.26.183`) and Ethernet source on all frames from this host |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** | NBNS name registration (`DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>`, `<20>`), NBT/browser host announcement, and NTLMSSP `hostname` field on outbound sessions |
| Windows domain | **NEMOTODES** (Kerberos realm `NEMOTODES.HEALTH`) | Kerberos AS/TGS exchanges, `kerberos.realm` field |
| Domain controller | 10.11.26.3, NetBIOS name `NEMOTODE-DC` | NBNS `<20>` registration, target of Kerberos/LDAP/SMB traffic from the victim |
| Logged-in domain user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ from 10.11.26.183, realm `NEMOTODES.HEALTH` |

Note: the AD DNS zone name resolved for SRV/LDAP lookups (`nemotoads.health`) differs by one letter from the Kerberos realm (`NEMOTODES.HEALTH`). Both spellings are genuinely present in the capture; this is called out for accuracy but has no bearing on the compromise.

The SMBv1/EFSR/NTLMSSP alerts against 10.11.26.3 are routine domain-joined-workstation traffic (Group Policy retrieval of `Registry.pol`/`GptTmpl.inf` from `\\10.11.26.3\SYSVOL`), not evidence of lateral movement by the malware.

## 2. Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** — the malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client as a remote-access trojan.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, on two independent grounds:
1. Suricata/ET rule hits directly naming it: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` / `Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
2. Independently verified in the raw packet payloads: outbound requests carry the literal HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` and use NetSupport's actual client protocol keywords in the request bodies — `CMD=POLL`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1`, and `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>` — POSTed to `/fakeurl.htm`, which is the documented NetSupport Manager check-in filename.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Command-and-control**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — NetSupport RAT C2. Traffic is **plaintext HTTP on port 443** (no TLS handshake to this host was observed), POSTing to `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` roughly every 60 seconds from 2024-11-26 08:50:45 through the end of the capture (09:43:29, ~53 minutes of sustained beaconing).

**Malicious/abused domains**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → **193.42.38.139** — landing/delivery domain; flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain` in both the DNS lookup and the TLS SNI. Large TLS sessions to this IP (~5.5 MB, ~2.8 MB, ~2.1 MB, and smaller ones) around 08:50:11–08:50:45 are consistent with an installer/payload download, immediately followed at 08:50:38 by a DNS lookup to `checkappexec.microsoft.com` (Windows SmartScreen app-execution reputation check), consistent with the user executing a just-downloaded file.
- `classicgrand.com` → **213.246.109.5** — upstream redirector/ad-chain domain visited immediately before `modandcrackedapk.com`.
- `confirmsubscription.com` → **52.8.34.0**, **13.56.30.207** — same redirect chain (fake-subscription/notification-prompt style domain), resolved in the same seconds as `modandcrackedapk.com`.
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → **104.26.1.231** / 104.26.0.231 / 172.67.68.212 — legitimate NetSupport Software infrastructure, but its use here (`GET /location/loca.asp`, returning `33.7488,-84.3877`) is the malicious client's built-in self-geolocation check, occurring seconds before the C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64 began.

**URLs observed in cleartext**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — C2 check-in/POST endpoint.
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` — geolocation lookup by the RAT client at startup.

**Transferred files / hashes**
- No file name or SHA256 hash could be extracted. The payload delivery from `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139) occurred entirely inside TLS sessions, and no TLS key log is present in this evidence set to decrypt them. The only artifacts recoverable in cleartext are the post-infection C2 protocol frames (`fakeurl.htm`) and the benign `loca.asp` geolocation response — neither is an executable. Do not treat this as "no file was dropped"; it means the capture alone cannot prove a hash, only that a large TLS transfer preceded RAT activity.

## 4. Summary Timeline (UTC+4 as captured)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 08:50:10–08:50:16 | Host browses through `classicgrand.com` → `confirmsubscription.com` / `modandcrackedapk.com` (mixed with benign font/CDN/maps loads typical of a landing page) |
| 08:50:38 | DNS query to `checkappexec.microsoft.com` (SmartScreen execution check) |
| 08:50:40 | Large TLS transfer from `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139); OCSP check to `r10.o.lencr.org` |
| 08:50:45 | DNS to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com`, `GET /location/loca.asp`; NetSupport RAT C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443 begins |
| 08:50:45 – 09:43:29 | Continuous ~60-second `POST /fakeurl.htm` check-ins to 194.180.191.64, confirmed by ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport signatures for the remainder of the capture |

**Recommendation:** Isolate DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183) from the network immediately, block 194.180.191.64, 193.42.38.139, 213.246.109.5, 52.8.34.0/13.56.30.207 and the associated domains at the perimeter, and reimage the host — NetSupport RAT provides full remote-hands access, so credentials used on this machine (including `oboomwald`'s domain account) should be considered exposed and rotated.
